rationale.usefulness: The documented SDK, run controls, session persistence and selectable execution environments address real needs in custom educational, website-maintenance and render-coordination apps. The article gives especially useful failure/recovery and operation-ID evaluation plans. Builders still need their own domain tools, UI, access design and model evaluation; the harness alone does not deliver the proposed artifacts.
rationale.impact: Decoupling clients, loop, providers and durable state is a meaningful contribution to operating agents as services. The evidence does not establish a new model capability, superior task performance or broad adoption, and no recovery/cost experiment was run. A moderate domain-impact score fits the demonstrated architectural utility.
rationale.novelty: The combination of local, standalone and Kubernetes paths with explicit session/run semantics, permission controls and transport limitations is practically differentiated. Durable state, leases, typed clients and orchestration are established infrastructure patterns. The source review does not establish uniquely new mechanisms or comparative superiority, so five is appropriate.
rationale.maturity: Detailed operator and SDK documentation provides a credible prototype path, but the project explicitly remains early. In-memory unauthenticated standalone defaults, non-exactly-once external effects, unfinished multi-user/cryptographic authority work and untested recovery are material readiness limits. This is below the midpoint for demonstrated reliable shared production use, despite the clear documentation.
rationale.openness: The inspected Apache-2.0 license, public harness source, Go embedding, documented gRPC/HTTP interfaces, TypeScript clients and multiple provider routes support substantial portability and inspection. An offline demo also helps inspect control flow without a paid model. External model terms, infrastructure and unfinished identity work limit end-to-end reproduction and keep this below exceptional openness.
